report.title: Dev Control engineering audit
report.scope: Read-only code, configuration, workflow, and aggregate runtime-observation audit of Dev Control. No production mutation, secret access, or destructive test was performed.
report.evidence_policy: Evidence cites repository paths and symbols at the source commit, plus explicitly labeled aggregate observations. It excludes secrets, personal data, raw logs, request payloads, tokens, and individual runtime records.
report.redaction_policy: All credentials, identifiers that could identify people, upload contents, raw runtime rows, host-specific paths, and notification destinations are omitted or described generically.

product_contract.intent: Dev Control is an operator-controlled system for planning, executing, validating, reviewing, and publishing repository changes. Existing merge and deploy behavior is intentional; remediation must harden its controls rather than remove those capabilities.
safety_invariants: Every externally visible state transition is attributable, durable, and recoverable.
A repair, review, merge, or deployment acts only on the approved, current immutable input and target revision.
The web process does not directly hold broad write or deployment authority when a durable job boundary can own it.
Public intake is validated, rate-limited, scoped, and cleaned up on every failure path.
Operational status distinguishes observations from guarantees and never silently masks verification failure.

official_references.topic: Claude Code CLI permissions and flags
Claude Code authentication and access management

source_checks.name: Scoped Vitest
source_checks.command: pnpm exec vitest run apps packages

source_checks.name: Unscoped Vitest
source_checks.result: also collects the separate .lfd harness, whose external credentials and fixtures were absent; this does not invalidate the scoped product test result

source_checks.name: CI test handling
source_checks.observation: Vitest is wrapped with a success-producing fallback, so CI can report success after test failure.

source_checks.name: Production dependency audit
source_checks.result: 15 production dependencies checked; zero known advisories

runtime_observations.redaction_note: Only aggregate counts are retained; no record identifiers, actor data, logs, payloads, or file paths are included.

summary.decision: Stabilize correctness, authority boundaries, and observability before workflow acceleration or autonomous policy expansion.
strengths: Queue claim uses a transaction and SKIP LOCKED.
Health and scoped test baselines were available at the audit point.
Deploy processing already records durable local state, deduplicates delivery identifiers, and validates webhook signatures.

groups.objective: Make jobs, deliveries, tickets, plans, and runs recoverable state machines with explicit ownership and idempotent rerun semantics.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G01-workflow-state. Implement durable workflow leases and a reaper without changing user-visible merge/deploy intent. Add job and delivery heartbeat/lease fields, reclaim only expired owned work, make related ticket/run transitions atomic, and return a new rerun identity after terminal work. Preserve history; never convert failed PR-review or conflict-resolution work to completed merely because a retry was queued. Add focused queue recovery tests and operator-visible recovery reasons.

groups.objective: Bind execution and publication to fresh isolated revisions with least-privilege agent tooling and reliable cleanup.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G02-execution-safety. Harden execution, repair, planning, and worktree lifecycle while retaining the current ability to publish valid changes. Clear or version result commits before repair; scan staged deletions safely; pass a scrubbed allowlist environment to validation and Claude; restrict Bash/Write permissions by operation; fetch and verify the configured starting revision; implement real cleanup; enforce scoped conflict edits; and guarantee planning timeout/finalization plus atomic plan-file/database persistence. Prove each behavior with small integration tests.

groups.objective: Ensure approval immutably binds the exact plan, configuration, prompts, skills, and model used by execution.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G03-approval-reproducibility. Make plan approval a compare-and-swap snapshot. Execute only the approved version, atomically lock its plan, prompt, project/config, skill, and model inputs, and retain rejection metadata. Apply required skills and documented ticket-override policy, distinguish harmless validation metadata changes from stale inputs, keep mandatory safety prompts enabled, preserve approved model overrides, version project imports, and replace brittle plan parsing with a compatible validated format. Add race and provenance tests.

groups.objective: Synchronize and act on GitHub pull-request truth with pagination, bounded transport, and immutable merge decisions.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G04-github-integrity. Create a bounded GitHub synchronization layer based on the official REST/GraphQL contracts. Use owner-qualified head filters and pagination, aggregate real review/check/requested-reviewer/diff/head data, add timeout/retry/backoff/version headers and custom-base support, and report stale state. Reject ambiguous verdict JSON. Bind merge to a freshly read unchanged head SHA plus enforced checks/reviews. Move write side effects from web requests into durable jobs and keep review retries state-preserving.

groups.objective: Retain automated deployment while binding it to approved master revisions, migration safety, health checks, rollback, and an auditable control plane.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G05-deployment-safety. Harden, do not remove, the current deploy webhook. Verify a successful required check belongs to the current protected master SHA; use frozen dependency installation; run migrations with an explicit failure policy; make release state atomic; add post-deploy health checks, rollback, approval/retry/history/audit records, and bounded recovery for corrupt or stuck state. Validate webhook size and external notification results, remove shell interpolation, and require explicit configured notification destinations.

groups.objective: Make public forms and uploads correctly validated, rate-limited, scoped, and recoverable.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G06-public-intake. Harden public intake with schema validation for every field type and option, optional email/URL correctness, HTTPS-only URLs, and correct radio/multiselect/static rendering. Either implement or visibly disable declared attachment/CAPTCHA/notification/rate-limit settings. Bind uploads to a short-lived form/session capability, atomically rate-limit attempts using trusted proxy configuration, verify multipart/image content, clean files after DB/user failures, expose authorized downloads, and reject ambiguous fallback project routing.

groups.objective: Reduce authority, harden HTTP/session boundaries, and keep credentials and error data out of insecure surfaces.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G07-auth-secrets. Establish least privilege across web, worker, deploy, and notification paths. Add baseline security headers; require production NODE_ENV and Secure cookies; use trusted-proxy-aware login throttling that avoids account lockout DoS; expire sessions; compare CSRF in constant time; encrypt or externalize notification authorization references; scrub errors/logs; remove password CLI leakage/truncation; and document a portable Argon2 build/runtime strategy. Move GitHub write/deploy authority out of the web process.

groups.objective: Deliver only configured events with durable, recoverable, idempotent notification processing.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G08-notifications. Make notification delivery operationally safe. Honor provider max_attempts, lease/recover sending deliveries, serialize manual retry against workers, route only events enabled by per-provider rules, complete event coverage, validate provider/endpoint/timeout configuration, forbid literal credentials, and make test/send operations idempotent with durable status transitions. Add provider contract tests and recovery tests without sending external messages.

groups.objective: Protect database and filesystem integrity through serialized migrations, enforceable invariants, atomic artifacts, retention, and tested restore.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G09-data-lifecycle. Make persistence authoritative. Add an advisory lock and unique migration naming policy; enforce workflow/status and append-only invariants in the database; transactionally coordinate plan artifacts with rows or use recoverable staging; review indexes against real query plans; back up database, filesystem artifacts, and configuration; implement documented retention/scheduling; and automate a restore drill that verifies an isolated restored service.

groups.objective: Expose accurate health, progress, logs, pagination, and error recovery guidance without mutation on read paths.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G10-operational-truth. Make operator surfaces truthful. Derive worker health from a renewable heartbeat rather than job claim time, validate GitHub authentication against the relevant capability, update run progress, show stale PR state, preserve historical log links on repair, paginate list/log APIs, make ticket-detail GET side-effect-free, return stable error codes with recovery steps, and remove or accurately label settings that advertise limits, cleanup, backups, or merge behavior not actually implemented.

groups.objective: Improve accessible, responsive, privacy-conscious operator and intake interfaces without redesigning the product surface.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G11-frontend-quality. Audit and correct the highest-impact frontend quality defects: keyboard tab semantics and focus management, mobile navigation semantics and touch targets, reduced-motion support, contrast verification, responsive labels for data tables, fixed-width overflow, and attachment visibility. Move inline styles/scripts toward CSP-compatible assets and evaluate local/system fonts for privacy and performance. Keep accent-border consistency as P3 unless user research elevates it.

groups.objective: Make verification trustworthy and reduce duplicated, oversized, or misleading maintenance surfaces.
groups.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for G12-ci-maintainability. Restore trustworthy delivery checks. Remove CI failure masking, define one documented root verification command, add focused route/worker/database/webhook/upload end-to-end coverage, and use the already-installed browser test tooling only where browser artifacts prove a real flow. Pin action/tool and production script versions, remove or implement placeholders/empty packages, consolidate duplicated resolvers, split oversized modules at tested seams, and document workspace prerequisites.

findings.title: Workflow ownership and terminal-state semantics are incomplete
findings.summary: Jobs can be claimed transactionally but lack renewable ownership and consistent state recovery semantics.
findings.impact: Work can strand after auth refusal or process loss, legitimate reruns can be blocked, and failed review/conflict work can be presented as completed.

evidence.observation: Claims record a time and worker but no lease heartbeat or reaper; idempotency conflict returns the existing row.
Authentication refusal and sequential worker flow require durable recovery semantics.

root_cause: No job or delivery lease, heartbeat, or reaper exists.
Authentication refusal can strand related tickets and runs.
Fixed idempotency keys return terminal jobs and block legitimate reruns.
PR-review and conflict retries can turn failed work into completed jobs.
Publication errors are swallowed.
State and event updates are not consistently atomic.
The worker is globally sequential despite UI claims.
Expired and stale operational records have no cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Add lease-backed transitions, a bounded reaper, explicit rerun identities, transactionally coupled events, and status-preserving retry rules.
acceptance_criteria: Only a live lease owner can complete or fail a job.
Expired work is recovered with an audit event and no duplicate publication.
A terminal run can be explicitly rerun without mutating history.
Retry never marks failed review/conflict work completed until its replacement succeeds.
interface_changes: Expose lease/recovery reason and immutable rerun linkage in operator APIs.

findings.title: Execution is insufficiently isolated from stale state and inherited authority
findings.summary: Repair/publication and Claude invocation paths can reuse stale commits, expose worker credentials, or exceed the intended operation scope.
findings.impact: A repair may publish an old commit; an agent or validation command can inherit authority beyond its task; planning artifacts can be orphaned.

evidence.observation: Execution and publication use stored result_commit/worktree state that must be reset and freshly bound for repairs.
Claude inherits process.env with an added OAuth token; execution enables Bash, Edit, and Write.
Worktree cleanup implementation is not a complete lifecycle guarantee.

root_cause: Repair attempts retain result_commit and can publish the old commit.
Staged deletions break secret scanning through git show :path.
Validation commands and Claude inherit sensitive worker credentials.
Claude Bash permissions are broader than prompt-only restrictions.
Execution can start from stale local default branches.
Cleanup scripts are placeholders.
The conflict resolver is prompted to edit while its tool allowance may not permit edits and it can modify unrelated paths.
Planning lacks reliable timeout/stream finalization and plan files can be orphaned before DB commit.
findings.recommendation: Create immutable attempt inputs, scrubbed environments, scoped tool policies, fresh revision checks, reliable artifact staging, and path-restricted conflict resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Repair cannot publish a prior attempt commit.
Secrets scanning handles deletions without reading invalid index paths.
Child processes receive only documented allowlisted variables.
Planning has a timeout, finalization record, and no orphan artifact after failure.
interface_changes: Persist immutable execution input/version and scoped operation policy metadata.

findings.title: Approval does not fully bind execution inputs
findings.summary: The approved plan and the worker's effective prompts, skills, and model can diverge.
findings.impact: An approved change may execute different instructions or configuration than the reviewer examined.

evidence.observation: Worker resolves execution inputs at runtime rather than from one immutable approved snapshot.
Plan acceptance depends on a rigid ordered-heading parser.

root_cause: Execution selects the earliest snapshot instead of the approved snapshot.
Approval status and race checks are incomplete.
Approval does not lock all prompt/project/model inputs.
Rejection leaves approval metadata.
Required skills and ticket override policy are ignored.
Validation metadata causes false staleness.
Mandatory safety prompts can be disabled.
Prompt provenance and preview differ from worker reality.
Approved model overrides are discarded.
Import-project updates bypass config versioning.
Rigid plan parsing has caused live failures.
findings.recommendation: Use an atomic approved-input snapshot with compare-and-swap approval, input hashes, provenance, and a tolerant structured plan contract.
acceptance_criteria: Execution reads exactly one approved snapshot.
Any material input mutation invalidates approval atomically.
Rejected plans retain rejection history but no active approval metadata.
Preview and worker resolve identical prompt/skill/model input hashes.
interface_changes: Add approved snapshot ID and input hashes to plan/execution APIs.

findings.title: GitHub synchronization and merge decisions are not authoritative enough
findings.summary: Provider calls are single-page, weakly bounded, and omit data needed for reliable review and merge policy.
findings.impact: The system can miss PRs, invent review/check truth, race a head update, or send direct write side effects from the web tier.

evidence.observation: Open-head lookup omits owner-qualified head syntax; list is one page; GraphQL hardcodes github.com; requests lack shared timeout/retry/version handling; merge does not bind an expected head SHA.

evidence.location: GitHub REST pull requests and pagination
evidence.observation: GitHub documents owner:ref head filtering and paginated list responses.

root_cause: Open-PR head filtering omits owner:.
List/sync paths do not paginate.
Review/check state is invented or absent instead of aggregated from proper APIs.
Requested reviewers and diff/head metadata are incomplete.
Aggressive polling lacks rate-limit/backoff/staleness behavior.
Requests lack timeout/retry/version handling.
GraphQL ignores custom API bases.
Environment fallback behavior contradicts docs.
Review retries are state-corrupting.
Verdict parsing accepts ambiguous JSON.
Merge decisions are not bound to unchanged head SHA and enforced checks/reviews.
Web owns write credentials and side effects instead of durable jobs.
findings.recommendation: Build a paginated, rate-aware, versioned sync adapter; materialize real policy inputs; and execute writes through jobs with final head/check/review verification.
acceptance_criteria: All pages are synced and stale data is labeled.
Merge rejects on changed head, missing required check, or missing review.
Review retries preserve prior failure history.
Web request handlers enqueue writes instead of performing provider mutations.
interface_changes: Expose source timestamp, page cursor, head SHA, required-check, and review-policy state.

findings.title: Deployment controls do not fully prove target, health, or recoverability
findings.summary: The webhook performs useful signature and CI checks but may deploy a successful ci check-run for a non-master SHA and deploy lacks migration/rollback controls.
findings.impact: An unintended revision can be released and a failed release can leave partial state without operator-grade recovery evidence.

evidence.observation: A successful check_run path passes its head SHA directly to deployment without proving it remains the protected branch head.
The script resets a target revision, runs non-frozen install, and restarts processes; it has no migration, post-health, or rollback step.

root_cause: Successful ci check-runs can deploy non-master SHAs.
Deploys do not run DB migrations.
Release update is non-atomic and lacks health checks/rollback.
Dependency install is not frozen.
Corrupt/stuck deploy state can reset or hang.
Webhook oversize and external response failures are mishandled.
Shell interpolation and a hardcoded phone fallback are unsafe.
Deployment history/approval/retry/audit are absent.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the webhook deploy flow but require protected-head verification, a staged release transaction, frozen install, migration/health/rollback gates, and durable audited deployment jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Only the current protected master SHA can deploy.
A release records approval, target, migration, health, and outcome.
Failed health check performs tested rollback or clearly blocks with recovery instructions.
No shell-interpolated deployment paths or implicit notification recipient remains.
interface_changes: Add deployment target, approval, health, rollback, and event history records.

findings.title: Public form validation, upload authorization, and failure cleanup are incomplete
findings.summary: Intake accepts values and upload capabilities with insufficient schema, authorization, and atomicity guarantees.
findings.impact: Attackers or malformed clients can bypass intended form rules, abuse uploads/rate limits, leave files behind, or silently route work to the wrong project.

evidence.observation: Form, rate-limit, multipart/image, proxy-IP, and upload lifecycle controls are concentrated in custom handlers and require complete trust-boundary coverage.

root_cause: Invalid optional email/URL values pass.
Field types/options are not fully validated.
URL schemes are unrestricted.
Radio/multiselect/static rendering is incorrect.
Form settings for attachments/CAPTCHA/notifications/rate limits are ignored or misleading.
Uploads are unauthenticated bearer UUIDs not bound to form/session.
Rate limiting counts accepted submissions only and is non-atomic.
Proxy IP handling is wrong.
Multipart/image checks are weak.
DB failure/or user failure leaves orphan files.
Attachment download is missing.
Fallback project assignment silently routes work.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a single validated form schema, bound upload capability, atomic attempt limiter, trusted proxy policy, and compensating file cleanup/download authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Optional invalid email/URL and non-HTTPS schemes fail validation when present.
Unsupported settings are rejected or accurately unavailable.
Uploads require short-lived scoped authorization and are cleaned after every failed path.
No fallback assignment occurs without explicit operator-visible selection.
interface_changes: Add scoped upload capability and explicit submission assignment outcome.

findings.title: Web and process boundaries hold excess authority and incomplete hardening
findings.summary: Session, error, credential, and process boundaries depend on environment discipline and broad web-process capability.
findings.impact: A deployment/configuration error or web compromise can weaken cookie security, expose secrets, or gain GitHub/deployment authority.

evidence.observation: Cookie Secure is conditional on NODE_ENV; CSRF comparison hashes then compares strings; login and provider configuration are web-tier trust boundaries.
Argon2 native build/runtime portability requires explicit operational support.

root_cause: Authenticated responses lack key security headers.
Production process config may omit NODE_ENV=production, leaving cookies without Secure.
Username lockouts enable denial of service and proxy IP handling is wrong.
Expired sessions are not cleaned.
CSRF comparison is not timing-safe.
Notification authorization secrets are stored as plaintext JSON.
Web holds GitHub write/deploy capability.
Error/secret redaction is narrow.
Password CLI input leaks/truncates edge cases.
Runtime Argon2 compilation is nonportable and undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Enforce production configuration, standard HTTP headers, constant-time token checks, expiry cleanup, secrets indirection/encryption, narrowed process roles, and portable password runtime documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Production boot fails closed without secure configuration.
Web process has no deploy or broad GitHub write credential.
Sensitive values are absent from returned errors and logs under tested failure cases.
Session and lockout controls resist timing and account-targeted DoS cases.
interface_changes: Add explicit process-role and secure-config health fields.

findings.title: Notification delivery is not fully policy-driven or recoverable
findings.summary: Delivery retries and provider selection do not yet enforce configuration, leases, or complete event routing.
findings.impact: Operators can receive duplicate, missing, or unintended notifications and stuck sends can persist.

evidence.observation: The event union contains a fixed subset of workflow events, and enqueueNotification inserts one delivery for every enabled provider with no provider-rule filter.
The worker claims queued/failed rows and marks them sending without a lease/heartbeat; retry scheduling increments attempts but does not read a provider max_attempts value.
The admin retry route calls provider.send directly, then updates the delivery without a compare-and-swap status guard or worker lease.
Configuration accepts authorization_header directly and endpoint validation only checks URL parseability; send uses the supplied method, headers, and timeout value.

root_cause: Provider max_attempts is ignored.
Manual retry can race and duplicate sends.
Sending deliveries have no recovery.
All providers receive all events because rule configuration is absent.
Event coverage is incomplete.
Provider/timeout/endpoint validation is weak.
Literal credentials are accepted.
Provider tests and sends lack robust idempotency/status checks.
findings.recommendation: Persist provider rules and delivery leases, validate configuration and secret references, and serialize retry/send transitions.
acceptance_criteria: A provider receives only enabled event types.
No two workers/manual actions can send one delivery concurrently.
Expired sending deliveries recover within configured attempts.
Provider test does not mutate normal delivery state.
interface_changes: Add provider event rules, delivery lease, and recovery reason fields.

findings.title: Persistence lifecycle lacks several database-enforced and restore-tested guarantees
findings.summary: Migrations, state records, filesystem artifacts, retention, and backups rely on conventions more than enforceable coordinated controls.
findings.impact: Concurrent migration or partial artifact failures can create divergent state, and recovery readiness is unproven.

evidence.observation: Runner records migrations without an advisory lock.
Migration prefix policy permits duplicated numeric prefixes.

root_cause: Migration runner lacks an advisory lock.
Migration prefixes are duplicated.
Status/data invariants lack DB checks.
Append-only records may still be deleted.
Plan files and DB writes are not atomic.
Indexes need query-driven review.
Backups omit filesystem artifacts/configuration and restore verification.
Advertised retention/scheduling is not implemented.
findings.recommendation: Serialize migrations, enforce data invariants and retention at the database boundary, use recoverable artifact staging, and prove complete restore.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent migration attempts serialize safely.
Invalid workflow transitions fail at the database layer.
Failed artifact write cannot leave an active plan pointing to missing content.
A documented restore drill restores DB, artifacts, and configuration into an isolated verification environment.
interface_changes: Add artifact state/manifest and restore-verification record types.

findings.title: Operator APIs and settings conflate activity, health, and claimed capability
findings.summary: Several health/progress/list/read paths do not accurately represent current system state or recovery options.
findings.impact: Operators can make unsafe decisions from stale or misleading dashboards and read requests can unexpectedly mutate workflow state.

evidence.observation: Worker heartbeat is derived from MAX(claimed_at), not a renewable worker signal.
Operator cards expose worker and queue state derived from activity queries.
Large route handler contains list/detail behavior and needs explicit side-effect-free read contracts.

root_cause: Worker health is hardcoded and job claim time is used as heartbeat.
Settings advertise nonexistent or mismatched limits, cleanup, backups, and disabled merge behavior.
GitHub auth health checks the wrong signal.
Run progress is never updated.
Stale PR state is hidden.
Repair overwrites log linkage so historical logs fail.
List/log APIs cap or load full data without pagination.
Ticket detail GET mutates status.
Errors often lack codes or actionable recovery.
findings.recommendation: Build health from renewable signals and capability probes; preserve history; paginate reads; and use stable errors/recovery metadata with side-effect-free GETs.
acceptance_criteria: Worker health expires without heartbeat.
GET requests do not change ticket state.
All list/log endpoints have documented pagination.
Every surfaced operational error includes a stable code and recovery action.
interface_changes: Add health freshness, progress, pagination cursor, stale-state, and recovery-code fields.

findings.title: Frontend accessibility and responsive quality require a targeted pass
findings.summary: Operator and public pages need keyboard, focus, motion, contrast, touch, responsive-data, attachment, CSP, and font improvements.
findings.impact: People using keyboard, touch, small screens, reduced motion, or constrained networks can lose context or be unable to complete workflows.

evidence.observation: Tab selection is wired to click events and toggles aria-selected/hidden panels, but the handler has no Arrow/Home/End keyboard navigation or focus movement.

evidence.symbol: dccPulse / dccIn keyframes and media rules
evidence.observation: The stylesheet defines pulse and dialog animations but has no prefers-reduced-motion override; its mobile rule hides list headers and uses generic ticket-row columns, while specialized table grids retain their desktop column definitions.
The form preview renders every non-static field as a disabled input, so attachment-specific presentation is not represented in the preview.
Every rendered document includes external Google Fonts links plus inline style and script content, which constrains a strict CSP and adds third-party font requests.
The mobile navigation trigger has an aria-label, but its click handler only toggles sidebar.open and the scrim; it does not expose expanded/controlled state or an Escape-key close path.

The mobile rules give common buttons, links, inputs, and the hamburger a 44px minimum height, but do not set a corresponding minimum width; skill-chip buttons have no component-specific target sizing.
CI runs installation, TypeScript, and Vitest only; it contains no browser or contrast-validation step for the design-token color combinations.

root_cause: Tab keyboard behavior, focus management, mobile navigation semantics, touch targets, reduced motion, contrast verification, and responsive data labeling need work.
Some fixed-width layouts overflow.
Attachments are not surfaced.
Inline scripts/styles complicate CSP.
External fonts add privacy/performance cost.
Lower-priority accent-border inconsistencies should remain P3.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize accessibility semantics and responsive content first, then isolate inline assets and evaluate font loading; retain minor accent-border cleanup as P3.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard tab/focus and modal flows pass manual accessibility checks.
Small-screen tables retain field labels and no horizontal page overflow at supported sizes.
Attachments are visible to authorized users.
Reduced-motion and contrast checks pass documented criteria.
interface_changes: Expose authorized attachment metadata to the relevant UI.

findings.title: CI masks failures and verification coverage does not cover critical boundaries
findings.summary: The baseline scoped tests pass, but CI intentionally converts Vitest failure to success and important route/worker/database/webhook/upload flows are not covered end to end.
findings.impact: Regressions can ship undetected and duplicated/oversized code increases drift and repair cost.

evidence.observation: Vitest is followed by a warning fallback that masks its exit status.
Large modules and duplicated resolver logic make boundary tests difficult.

root_cause: CI explicitly masks Vitest failures.
No root verification script or meaningful route/worker/database/webhook/upload E2E coverage exists.
Playwright is installed but unused.
Action/tool versions and production scripts are not reproducible.
Placeholder scripts and empty packages mislead.
Duplicated web/worker resolvers have already drifted.
Very large server/worker/UI modules inhibit testing.
Workspace dependency declarations and setup prerequisites are incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Make CI fail honestly, establish one root verification command, target high-risk boundary coverage, and reduce drift through small shared tested seams and reproducible tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A failing test fails CI.
One documented local command runs lint/type/test contract checks.
Critical route, worker, database, webhook, and upload journeys have meaningful automated coverage.
Tool/action versions and setup prerequisites are pinned and documented.
interface_changes: Publish a root verification command and environment prerequisites contract.

roadmap.goal: Stop false success and make current state observable before expanding behavior.

items.name: Truthful verification and operational baseline
acceptance_criteria: Scoped Vitest remains green and CI no longer masks failures
operator read APIs are side-effect-free

Remove only the CI success-masking fallback, add one documented root verification script using existing tools, and add focused checks for side-effect-free reads and truthful health/error fields. Do not add dependencies or change deployment behavior.

acceptance_criteria: expired work recovers audibly
web no longer carries deploy/broad write authority

Create one shared project preflight that validates repository revision, agent start path, configured skills/prompts, required environment, and runtime prerequisites. Return a structured immutable result used by planning and execution; reuse existing project-config capabilities.

acceptance_criteria: all pages sync
stale state is visible

items.agent_prompt: Use docs/audit/dev-control-audit.json as the canonical audit contract for R2-01. Build a minimal deployment control center around the existing deploy flow: protected-head verification, frozen install, migration policy, health checks, history, explicit approval/retry, and rollback. Do not remove automated deployment; make every decision durable and visible.

items.name: Backup and restore drills
